description: The space of positive integers under the Collatz map can be viewed as a fitness landscape where 'fitness' = delay D(n). Delay records are peaks in this landscape. The landscape has fractal structure with self-similar ridges corresponding to numbers sharing residue families. Evolution on this landscape via mutation (incrementing n) and selection (keeping high-delay numbers) mirrors biological adaptive walks.
mathematical_formalization: Define fitness f(n) = D(n). The 'mutational neighborhood' of n is {n-1, n+1, 2n, n/2 if even}. A 'ridge' is a maximal connected set of numbers with D(n) > D(m) for all m not on the ridge with m < max(ridge). Known ridges correspond to residue families sharing the same Res(n) value.
analogical_connections: Wright's adaptive landscape: delay records are 'fitness peaks' separated by 'valleys' of low-delay numbers
Kauffman's NK model: the ruggedness of the Collatz fitness landscape depends on the coupling between binary digits
Spin glass models in physics: the Collatz landscape has quenched disorder from the interplay of 3x+1 and x/2
implementation_hypothesis: Implement a genetic algorithm that evolves populations of integers, using delay as fitness, with mutations being bit-flips in binary representation. Compare GA convergence to the known delay record list.
experiment_seed: Map the local fitness landscape around each known delay record by computing D(n) for n in [record-1000, record+1000]. Characterize the typical 'peak shape' and 'valley depth'.
